items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: Rossini is mentioned only as a composer of operas (e.g., 'Barbara Seville', 'more of Rossini') performed in New Orleans theaters during the 1820s-1830s, long before the interviewee's active career.

ctx.x: Well, what about the rest of the country, as compared with New Orleans, as far as general musical sophistication is concerned? Both Negro and white, I'm talking about.

Well, it depends on the period you're talking about. In the, uh, pre-Civil War period, New Orleans is unmistakably miles ahead of the rest of the United States. It is a musical center in the United States. No question about that. And, uh, this was not exclusive with the whites. There were a great many Negro musicians who were taught by the white musicians playing in the French Opera, and in, uh, uh, the St. Charles Theater Orchestra, which was a very, very fine orchestra, uh, also. And these Negro musicians, in…
But they had academic music games, they mostly in the form of opera? That was the principal academic music, opera.
